find: const target: Tank | null = threats.engagedInSight ? threats.engaged : null;
killedBy: issue #893: one opponent drives movement AND fire, not two holds its turret when NOTHING is visible, rather than tracking the tank behind the wall
why: Drops the line-of-sight half of the firing gate. `engaged` falls back to the nearest opponent when none is visible, so without this test a bot acquires a firing solution on a tank behind a wall: `hasSolution` goes true, the reaction clock runs, and the bot shoots into the wall it is driving toward. This is the half of `engaged = nearestVisible ?? nearest` that keeps the unification a refactor rather than a lethality change -- the fallback exists to give MOVEMENT an opponent when nothing is visible, never to give firing one.
